questions.question: Which generation of programming languages uses mnemonics and requires an assembler?
questions.explanation: 2nd generation languages are assembly languages using mnemonics; 1st generation is machine/binary language.

questions.concept: Error-correcting codes as a TOC application
questions.question: Which of the following is listed as an application of Theory of Computation?
questions.explanation: Applications listed include cryptography, algorithm design, quantum calculation, correcting errors in codes, string pattern matching, compiler design and AI.

questions.question: Which malicious software gives an attacker administrative access while hiding its own presence on the system?
questions.explanation: Rootkits provide administrative access along with stealth capability, hiding malicious activity.

questions.question: In the seven steps of machine learning, which step comes immediately before Training?
questions.explanation: The order is Gathering data, Preparing data, Choosing a model, Training, Evaluation, Hyperparameter tuning, Prediction.

questions.concept: Frame number bits for 64 KB physical memory
questions.question: Physical memory is 64 KB and the frame size is 1 KB. How many bits does the physical address use for the frame number?
questions.explanation: 64 KB = 2^16, so the physical address is 16 bits. The offset for 1 KB is 10 bits, leaving 16 - 10 = 6 bits for the frame number (64 frames).

questions.question: Which subnet mask allows exactly 2 usable hosts?
questions.explanation: 252 leaves 2 host bits: 2^2 - 2 = 2 hosts; 248 gives 6 and 240 gives 14.

questions.question: In object-oriented programming, abstraction refers to:

options.A: Giving one function name more than one form
options.B: Deriving a new class from an existing class
options.C: Hiding the implementation and showing only the features
options.D: Binding data and functions into a single unit

questions.explanation: Abstraction hides implementation details and exposes only the essential features. Binding data and functions is encapsulation, deriving classes is inheritance and many forms is polymorphism.

questions.question: Which of the following are listed as Network layer protocols? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: ARP, RARP, ICMP and IGMP are Network layer protocols; SLIP is Data Link and MIME is Presentation.

questions.question: Who is credited with creating the MQTT protocol?
questions.explanation: MQTT was created by Andy Stanford-Clark and is associated with IBM. Berners-Lee and Cailliau are linked to the WWW and Vint Cerf to the Internet.

questions.concept: BFS preferred when target is near source
questions.question: When the target vertex is expected to be close to the source vertex, which traversal is generally better?

options.B: BFS, because it uses a stack
options.C: BFS, because it explores level by level using a queue
options.D: DFS, because it uses a queue

questions.explanation: BFS uses a queue and is better when the target is close to the source; DFS (stack/recursion) is better when the target is far.

questions.concept: Number of phases in RAD model
questions.question: The RAD (Rapid Application Development) model is organised into how many phases?
questions.explanation: As per the syllabus, the RAD model has 5 phases.

questions.concept: Shared printer requests as queue application
questions.question: Which of the following is an application of a queue rather than a stack?

options.A: Handling requests sent to a shared printer
options.C: Matching nested parentheses in an expression

questions.explanation: Shared printer requests are served first come first served, which is FIFO queue behaviour. Undo/redo, parenthesis matching and string reversal are stack applications.

questions.concept: Negative index maps to positive index
questions.question: Given str1 = 'Hello World!', what does str1[-6] return?
questions.explanation: The string has 12 characters, so index -6 is the same as index 12 - 6 = 6, which is 'W'.

questions.question: What was the original name of SQL?
questions.explanation: SQL was originally called SEQUEL, Structured English Query Language.

questions.question: Which software is primarily used to create vector images?
questions.explanation: Adobe Illustrator and CorelDraw are vector tools; Photoshop is pixel-based.

questions.question: Match each situation with the most suitable model: (i) a 150-line programming exercise, (ii) a project whose team lacks experience on similar projects and needs risk analysis, (iii) a project where the user is involved in every phase. Which mapping is correct?
questions.explanation: Build and Fix suits exercises of about 100-200 LOC, spiral suits inexperienced teams and includes risk analysis, and prototyping suits full user involvement.

questions.concept: VPN as a cyber security tool
questions.question: Which of the following is a cyber security tool rather than a threat?
questions.explanation: Cyber security tools include antivirus, antimalware, encryption tools, VPN and strong passwords; keyloggers, botnets and rootkits are threats.

questions.concept: Matching except clause among multiple handlers
questions.explanation: Accessing index 5 of a two-element list raises IndexError. Only the first matching handler runs, so just 'I' is printed.

questions.question: What is the role of the dispatcher in process management?

options.A: It loads new processes from disk into RAM
options.B: It gives the CPU to the process selected by the short-term scheduler
options.C: It de-allocates the resources of terminated processes
options.D: It swaps processes between RAM and secondary memory

questions.explanation: The dispatcher allocates the CPU to the process chosen by the short-term scheduler. Swapping is the medium-term scheduler's job.

questions.question: What is the basic memory element in a digital circuit?
questions.explanation: A flip-flop is a bistable sequential circuit that stores one bit and is the basic memory element.

questions.question: A user's previously granted access to a table must be withdrawn. Which SQL command is used?
questions.explanation: REVOKE is a DCL command that removes authorization granted with GRANT; ROLLBACK undoes transaction changes.

questions.question: Which of the following names CANNOT be used as an identifier in Python?
questions.explanation: nonlocal is a reserved keyword. Keywords are case-sensitive, so TRUE is not the keyword True, and Pass_1 and _None are ordinary valid names.

questions.concept: Output function not part of TM 7-tuple
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the components of the Turing machine 7-tuple?
questions.explanation: The TM 7-tuple has Q, two alphabets, delta, q0, B and F; the output function lambda belongs to Moore and Mealy machines.

questions.question: Which is the correct HTML code to create an e-mail link?
questions.explanation: E-mail links use the anchor tag with the mailto: scheme in href.
